text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danish police have decided to double their representation at Europol's headquarters in The Hague to two employees. The second officer will work on the European biker surveillance project intitiated and run by Denmark.

--- Part of the Nordisk Film group, Nordisk Film Home Entertainment, and one of the world's largest distributors of computer games Virgin Interactive Entertainment have agreed to make Nordisk Film Home Entertainment exclusive distributor of Virgin computer games in Scandinavia.

--- Toy group Lego's new entertainment park in Windsor close to London had close to 1.4 million visitors in its first season ending in a few weeks. The 740 million crown park has increased sales of Lego in Britain by 10-20 percent which is more than in any other European country.

--- Technology company Chartec Laboratories which has invented a new and popular type of battery recharger plans to enter the Copenhagen stock market next year. Chartec expects the offering to raise 200 to 300 million crowns in extra share capital.

--- Dairy advertising campaigns on ecological products have increased sales of products under the name of Harmonie. MD Foods and Kloever Maelk have together sold close to 60 percent of the 95 million litres of ecological milk produced each year and which now represent more than 10 percent of the total sales of milk.

--- A trade ministry report now concludes that export companies with less than 100 employees have problems adapting to larger and more international markets. From 1985 to 1993 exports in small and newly established companies decreased from 1 billion crowns to 430 million crowns.
